story.what_it_does: Kajaria Ceramics makes and sells tiles, which brought in about ₹4,280 crore of its roughly ₹4,832 crore FY26 revenue. It also sells bathware and adhesives, and has a Nepal joint venture.
story.plans: It is adding capacity: a brownfield expansion at Srikalahasti (12.5 million sq m, targeted for end of June next year) and a new line at Gailpur, Rajasthan. The Erode adhesive plant started production in May 2026, and management targets about ₹400 crore of adhesive revenue in FY28 and double-digit volume growth over the next two quarters.
story.moat: The notes show no explicit moat statement, but the company has scale across tiles, bathware and adhesives and was able to raise prices about 12-13% after gas costs rose. Margins rose from 12.8% to around 19.5%, though management gave only vague answers on gross margin.

scenarios.story: Price hikes stick and volumes keep growing at double digits, with new Srikalahasti and Gailpur capacity and adhesives adding to sales. Margins stay near 19% and operating EBITDA passes ₹1,000 crore.
signals_to_watch: Volume growth staying at 10% or more in the next two quarters
EBITDA margin holding at 18-19% for FY27

scenarios.story: Revenue growth stays strong near-term on higher prices, with volumes growing at a moderate pace and margins in the 18-19% range. Capacity additions arrive roughly on schedule, though bathware stays tough.
signals_to_watch: Srikalahasti commissioning by end of June next year
Working capital cycle staying near 46-51 days

scenarios.story: Morbi plants restarting and outsourcing supply could raise competition and erode pricing, while gas stays costly and hard to get. Margins could slip if price hikes reverse or volumes disappoint.
signals_to_watch: Gas availability and cost, which management said will be tough going forward
Volume growth falling below double digits, as in April 2026
